subject: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@fincorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up and next steps

Hi Beth —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view:

Summary of needs we heard:
- Private connectivity from FinCorp VPC to Redwood Private endpoints (VPC endpoints or peering)
- IP allowlist + outbound egress controls for tokenized requests
- DNS resolution for Redwood endpoints (private DNS or custom zone)
- mTLS for service-to-service auth (preferred) or customer-managed TLS certs
- Auth: mutual TLS for infra calls, API keys scoped per service for app-level calls
- SDK setup: server-side SDK in our backend, client-side callers should never hold long-lived keys
- Structured output / tool calling: need stable JSON schemas and webhook endpoints for tool execution
- Embeddings/reranker: want to push embeddings to your vector store or use Redwood-hosted embeddings with private routing

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Marissa/Jonas: can you share the VPC endpoint hostnames + IP ranges we should expect to allow? Also capture TLS/mTLS flow and whether Redwood will terminate mTLS at the endpoint. (Marissa: assigning to you)
2) Beth/Alex: confirm whether FinCorp prefers VPC endpoint peering vs. managed interface endpoints and whether you have a private DNS zone we can add records to.
3) I'll schedule a 30-min integration call for early next week (include infra + engineering folks) to walk through the network diagram and auth flow.
4) I'll attach a starting architecture diagram and an example IP allowlist CSV for your infra team.

Attachments: fincorp-redwood-integration-diagram.pdf (high-level), vpc-endpoint-ip-list.csv (example)

Thanks — looking forward to lining this up.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Beth Carter <beth.carter@fincorp.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fincorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up and next steps

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the integration call:

1) We'll likely prefer interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) over peering for isolation, but I need to confirm with infra.
2) For DNS, we run a private hosted zone (internal.fincorp) and can add A/CNAME records if you provide the hostnames.
3) For mTLS: security would prefer mutual TLS terminated at our edge with client certs from Redwood. Is that supported or does Redwood expect to terminate mTLS on the Redwood side?
4) Embeddings: we would like to keep vector storage inside our VPC (self-hosted vector DB). Can Redwood route embedding generation calls to return vectors so we can store them locally, or do you propose a direct bulk export?

Also please include any minimal firewall rules (port/protocol) we need to allow outbound. Looking forward to the integration call — Alex and I are available Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Cheers,
Beth
Beth Carter
Head of Integrations, FinCorp
beth.carter@fincorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@fincorp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up and next steps

Hi Beth / Lauren —

Thanks — looping in the infra details below. I pulled this together based on our Private offering and what we've delivered for other enterprise customers.

Network endpoints / IPs:
- Primary Redwood Private endpoint hostnames (regional):
  - us-west-2.api.redwood-inference.private
  - us-east-1.api.redwood-inference.private
- Current egress IP ranges (examples): 54.143.10.0/24, 52.12.48.0/24 — we'll provide a full CSV exported for your firewall team (attached: vpc-endpoint-ip-list.csv).
- Protocols/ports: outbound TCP 443 (HTTPS) is sufficient for all API calls. If you use gRPC streaming, still over 443.

DNS / private zone:
- We can support private DNS via conditional forwarding or by providing A/CNAME records for your private hosted zone. If you prefer, we can supply SRV records for region routing.

mTLS / TLS termination:
- Redwood supports both models:
  1) Redwood-terminated mTLS: we present client certs to Redwood and Redwood validates. This simplifies our auth flow and allows centralized rotation.
  2) Customer-terminated mTLS: if FinCorp requires client certs to be validated at your edge, we can arrange mutual cert negotiation and then forward traffic over a private link. In that case, we'd rely on JWTs or short-lived API tokens between your edge and Redwood for identity.
- Let us know which you prefer; we can provide sample certs and an mTLS handshake diagram on the call.

Auth options / SDK notes:
- Recommended: server-to-server calls use mTLS for network-level auth + short-lived bearer tokens (OAuth2) issued by Redwood. App-level usage should call your backend which then proxies to Redwood (do not embed keys in client apps).
- Our server-side SDKs (Node/Python/Go) support automatic token refresh and built-in retry with idempotency for request replay. We will share a quickstart repo on the integration call.

Embeddings / reranker flow:
- Option A (preferred for security): Redwood generates embeddings inside Private deployment, returns vectors in-line over the connection; you push vectors directly to your vector DB (we can stream batched payloads).
- Option B: Redwood hosts vector storage in a private tenant and exposes an API your infra can call to fetch or sync vectors (we can set up role-based access).
- Both approaches support cosine/inner-product exports; reranking can be done client-side or via Redwood's reranker endpoint over the same secure link.

Structured output / tool calling:
- For tool calling, we recommend using our webhook-based action runner behind your private endpoint. Redwood will emit structured JSON per the agreed schema; your runner can validate and execute with the provided signatures.
- We will provide a sample JSON schema and an example webhook verification flow (HMAC or mTLS-backed).

Attachments & links:
- Attached: vpc-endpoint-ip-list.csv (authoritative IP list for infra)
- Architecture diagram in shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-IntegrationDocs

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm interface endpoint preference (PrivateLink) and provide a point-of-contact for infra to receive the CSV.
- We schedule a 30-min deep-dive with FinCorp infra + Redwood infra (Jonas + me) Tuesday 4/27 2:30pm PST.

If anything here looks off, let me know and I'll adjust prior to the call.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Integration Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fincorp.com>

Subject: Re: VPC connectivity - integration follow-up and next steps

Marissa / Lauren —

Thanks for the details. Confirming FinCorp prefers interface endpoints (PrivateLink) and we can add A records in internal.fincorp once you provide hostnames. Tue 4/27 2:30pm PST works for infra folks.

I'll have our infra engineer onboard the call; we have no objection to mTLS terminated at Redwood as long as we get client cert rotation details. For embeddings, we'll test Option A (generate and return vectors over the private link) and plan to store them in our internal vector DB.

I'll accept the calendar invite when it's sent.

— Alex
